dialogue.spoken_text: Hi! Follow the Collatz sequence through our number waterworks.
Start with a positive whole number. These two rules make the next number.
Even? Divide by two. Eight divided by two is four.
Odd? Multiply by three, then add one. Five times three, plus one, is sixteen.
These mirrors show number values, not amounts of water. Three copies mean three times the value.
Let's start with seven, and stop when we reach one.
Seven reached one in sixteen steps. Now start a new trip at twenty-seven.
Three twenty-sevens make eighty-one. Add one: eighty-two. Eighty-one belongs inside the calculation; it is not a sequence entry.
Four digits! The same rule still works. Three equal copies, then one extra.
The highest value on this trip! Now watch the even rule bring it down.
A familiar ending! Follow every step again. The same value always uses the same rule.
Both trips reached one. If we continued, one would go to four, then two, then one again.
Does every positive whole number reach one? That is the Collatz conjecture. It has not been proved for all numbers.
Two rules, and a surprising journey. Thanks for counting with me!
